name: Tombstone
manufacturer: Various; recipe originating from Shelf chemist 'Pala Voss'
description: A cocktail of expired veterinary tranquilizers — primarily tiletamine and zolazepam recovered from black-market animal control stockpiles — dissolved in pharmaceutical-grade ethanol and stabilized with crushed expired Nullocaine tablets. Produces a profound dissociative state that Shelf residents describe as 'being dead for a while' — complete emotional and physical detachment, near-catatonia, with dreamlike internal experiences. Used heavily as an escape drug in the worst parts of the Shelf.
effects: vivid internal dream-state while appearing catatonic
temporary cessation of anxiety and trauma response
side_effects: severe emergence agitation (violent confusion on waking)
prolonged dissociative episodes lasting beyond intended duration
cultural_context: Tombstone is understood even by Shelf residents as a drug of last resort — the thing you take when you can't bear being present in your own life anymore. There's no glamour to it. Entire blocks in the lower Shelf have informal 'watchers' — people who sit with users to make sure they keep breathing. The name isn't ironic. Tombstone users are nicknamed 'markers' by neighbors who check on them.
story_hooks: A watcher has been found dead alongside three Tombstone users — someone tampered with a batch, and the question is whether it was deliberate targeting or sloppy cutting
A Tier 3 social worker who went undercover in the Shelf to document Tombstone use has gone missing — last seen heading toward a known distribution point
Pala Voss, the original chemist, is still alive and has developed a harm-reduction version of the formula — she's trying to get it distributed but someone is blocking her
